# `recursive-call`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: disciplined · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports direct recursion and proven two-function mutual recursion in the scanned
project.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Recursion makes stack consumption depend on input depth; an explicit worklist
makes the resource visible and boundable.

## When it fires

An unqualified call names the declaration visible where it is made: the
function of that name in the innermost enclosing container, so two `format`
methods of different types, or a method and a file-level function sharing a
name, are different functions. A call must also pass as many arguments as the
function takes; one that does not cannot be to it (it sits in a branch
`comptime` discards). Reported mutual cycles name both functions, which are
declared in the same file.

Recursion no runtime input can deepen is exempt: `inline` functions, functions
returning `type`, `comptime_int`, or `comptime_float` (every call runs at
compile time), functions whose parameters are all `comptime` (no runtime
argument reaches them), and calls inside `comptime` blocks or expressions. So
is recursion over a type: every recursive call sits in a prong of a
`switch (@typeInfo(...))` other than `.pointer` and dereferences nothing, as
`std.hash.autoHash` and `std.mem.doNotOptimizeAway` recurse into a field,
element, payload or integer conversion of their argument, so the depth is the
nesting of the type. Recursion that follows a pointer can reach the same type
again and is still reported, as is other recursion through `anytype`
parameters.

So is recursion an explicit bound limits: the function checks a depth counter
that every recursive call advances (`if (depth >= 32) return false;` and
`walk(child, depth + 1)`), or a budget it passes on, where failing the check
leaves the function (`try require(remaining.* != 0)`,
`budget.charge(depth) catch return false`). A budget is a pointer named
`budget`, `remaining` or `fuel`, typed `*...Budget`, or an integer the body
counts down. A counter passed by value and counted down to its check
(`if (remaining == 0) return null;` and `visit(..., remaining - 1)`) bounds the
depth by its starting value: a private function whose callers in its file all
start it from an integer literal or a container-level constant is exempt;
otherwise, as for `fact(n - 1)`, the finding names the counter and says that
callers choose the depth. A call that reduces a parameter below the guard
leading to it, `if (shift >= limb_bits)` then `llshl(r, a, shift % limb_bits)`,
recurses only once. A cursor counting up through the input is input-controlled
and still reported. Like the other disciplined-profile rules it skips `test`
blocks, private functions only tests call, and test, fuzz, and script files.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn fact(n: u64) u64 {
    if (n == 0) return 1;
    return n * fact(n - 1);
}
```
